claim: Asymptotically, 1-nearest-neighbour retrieval errs at most about twice the Bayes error (2R*(1-R*) for two classes). This is a large-sample guarantee only and says nothing about small case bases, irrelevant features or the metric.
agent_test: Not testable at agent scale; treat similarity retrieval as a floor, not a ceiling.

claim: Storing only misclassified cases (IB2) saves storage but stores noise: at 10% noise IB2 kept 26.3% noisy instances while IB3 (per-case accuracy record with significance test) kept 0. Keep-what-you-got-wrong retention is fragile under noisy feedback. Update: Xiong et al. 2025 found add-all memory lowers agent success by 8 to 12 points vs a fixed 100-record memory in 4 agents, so keep-everything is worse than keep-verified.
agent_test: Fill the case bank by failure-only vs verified-success-only storage with 10% corrupted outcome labels, at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieving the nearest examples by embedding similarity beats random in-context examples for GPT-3 (KATE): IMDB 91.99 vs 87.95 random; NQ EM about 41 vs 28.6; nearest-10 EM 46.0 vs farthest-10 31.0 on 100 questions. Random sets also vary a lot (SST-2 86.9 to 95.8).
agent_test: Equal-token ablation on our agent: nearest-k vs random-k vs farthest-k stored cases on held-out tasks.

claim: No exact replication of KATE was found, but later work (EPR, CEIL, UDR, Dr.ICL) reproduces the direction (similarity retrieval beats random) with other models and tasks. Random baselines are very low on structured outputs (1.7 to 8.9 in EPR).
agent_test: Always include a random-case control; do not trust a retrieval gain without it.
audit_note: Minor: UDR was not among the listed sources; EPR random 1.7/7.3/8.9 (BREAK/MTOP/SMCalFlow) and CEIL random 30.68 vs BM25 45.84 match; 'no exact replication found' is a negative search claim that cannot be checked from the sources.

claim: Which encoder defines similarity matters. Encoders tuned on a task-like objective help (SST-2 tuned 93.43) and ones tuned on a dissimilar objective can hurt (NLI/STS-B 90.2 to 90.4 vs roberta 91.99). Plain kNN label voting (50.2 on IMDB) is near chance, so the LLM reading the cases does the work.
agent_test: Compare cosine over task text vs over plan text vs over outcome summary as case keys.

claim: Lexical overlap (BM25) beats dense SBERT as an unsupervised case retriever for structured-output tasks (dev BREAK 26.0 vs 21.6, MTOP 52.9 vs 48.7, SMCalFlow 46.1 vs 43.6, GPT-Neo 2.7B), and BM25 is a robust baseline out of domain on BEIR. Learned dense retrieval wins on open-domain QA (RAG).
agent_test: Test a BM25 key vs dense key vs hybrid for retrieving prior solved problems; BM25 costs no tokens.

claim: A retriever trained on LM-scored usefulness (EPR) beats surface similarity: BREAK 31.9 vs 26.0, MTOP 64.2 vs 57.0, SMCalFlow 54.3 vs 51.4 (dev, GPT-Neo), and matches or beats a BM25 oracle that sees the gold output on MTOP and SMCalFlow. UDR, LLM-R and CEIL extend this.
agent_test: Log which stored cases, when shown, led to a verified solve; re-rank retrieval by that outcome score.
audit_note: Minor: the comparison numbers MTOP 57.0 and SMCalFlow 51.4 are CBR, a supervised retriever, not surface similarity (BM25 is 52.9 and 46.1); BREAK 31.9 vs BM25-oracle 32.3 is a near tie.

claim: Set-level selection beats one-by-one similarity: CEIL averages 56.76 over 12 datasets vs EPR 53.37, TopK-BM25 45.84, Random 30.68 (GPT-Neo 2.7B). Gains are largest on generation and NLI, under 1 point on CommonsenseQA and HellaSwag.
agent_test: Compare top-k similarity vs a relevance-times-diversity set (MMR) at k=3, equal tokens.

claim: Diversity helps when no single stored case is close: Levy et al. report 50.3 to 73.5 on SMCalFlow-CS 32-C (top-K vs Cover-LS) and wins on 7 of 8 compositional splits. Boundaries read in the paper: Cover-LS scored 0.3 on the zero-shot 0-C split where top-K got 17.0, and on COVR-10 random (69.4) beat top-K (61.8).
agent_test: When the best cached case has low similarity, switch from top-k to a diverse set or to no case; measure it.

claim: Diversity is not free: on easy or high-zero-shot tasks pure similarity wins or ties (Llama-3.1-8B SST-2 TopK 94.13 vs TopK-Div 92.75; GSM8K TopK 81.74 vs TopK-Div 82.98, a gap of about 1 point); it helps harder tasks (SQuAD 73.28 to 77.71). MMR reranking matches or beats the similarity baseline in 17 of 24 settings (about 70%), with gains from 0 to over 9 percent depending on dataset.
agent_test: Gate diverse retrieval on problem difficulty; use top-1 for easy items.
audit_note: SST-2 94.13 vs 92.75 and SQuAD 73.28 to 77.71 match Xiao et al.; Kapuriya et al. report MMR outperforms or matches the similarity baseline in 17 of 24 settings, so 'helps in about 70%' counts ties as help, and 'mostly by small amounts' is not stated (COLA gains reach +9.7%). On GSM8K TopK-Div (82.98) is slightly above TopK (81.74).
claim_before_audit: Diversity is not free: on easy or high-zero-shot tasks pure similarity wins or ties (Llama-3.1-8B SST-2 TopK 94.13 vs TopK-Div 92.75; GSM8K gaps about 1 point); it helps harder tasks (SQuAD 73.28 to 77.71). MMR rerank helps in about 70% of configurations, mostly by small amounts.

claim: Labels in fixed random demonstrations matter less than expected: random labels cost 0-5% absolute (mean 2.6 classification, 1.7 multi-choice; 12 models, verified in the paper). Demos mainly give format, label space and input distribution. This is not shown for retrieved near-duplicates, where label copying is plausible. Update: Yoo et al. 2022 found label correctness matters more or less depending on template and model size; Xiong et al. 2025 found agents copy similar retrieved records and wrong stored runs propagate. Still no corrupted-label test on retrieved cases with a frontier model.
agent_test: Give retrieved near-duplicate cases with correct vs corrupted solutions; a drop shows the agent copies.

claim: Models copy from top-ranked retrieved prompts: on MTOP 84.5% of outputs abstractly matched a retrieved prompt, with 71.6 EM on that subset vs 64.2 overall. Update: Xiong et al. 2025 (4 agents, GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 too) show output similarity rises with input similarity (experience-following), so the copying also holds for agents.
agent_test: Measure how often final answers copy structure from the top case, and accuracy when copied vs not.
audit_note: Minor: EPR 'copied' means an abstract (structure) match with a retrieved prompt; Xiong et al. show output similarity rising with input similarity on several agents and backbones (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3 in the appendix), which supports but is not identical to copying.

claim: In agent settings the best number of retrieved cases is small. Memento F1/PM: K=0 59.9/72.2, K=1 63.6/77.9, K=4 64.5/78.5 (best), K=32 63.9/78.1 (verified). ReasoningBank (verified): k=0 39.0, k=1 49.7, k=2 46.0, k=3 45.5, k=4 44.4 on WebArena-Shopping. Beyond K=1 differences are within noise or negative.
agent_test: Sweep k in {0,1,2,4,8} at equal total tokens; expect most gain at k=1.
audit_note: Minor: 'differences within noise' beyond K=1 for Memento (63.6 to 64.5 F1) is an interpretation, since no confidence intervals are reported; Memento's best is K=4, not K=1, and two systems are a thin base for 'agent settings' generally.

claim: Case memory helps most out of distribution: Memento +4.7 to +9.6 OOD but only +0.4 (non-parametric) and +1.0 (parametric) in distribution at iteration 5 on DeepResearcher; the bank saturates near 3k items.
agent_test: Split eval into seen-type and unseen-type problems and report case-memory gain on each.

claim: Self-generated successful trajectories retrieved by similarity improve agents without training: ALFWorld 73 to 89 (93 with curation), Wordcraft 55 to 64, InterCode-SQL 75 to 79 (gpt-4o-mini); ExpeL ALFWorld task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs ReAct 40.0, random successes 42.5, reasoning-step similarity 48.5 (verified). Naive accumulation is unstable and marginal value falls with bank size.
agent_test: Compare store-all vs verified-success-only vs curated bank over 5 seeds at equal tokens.

claim: What is stored matters as much as how it is retrieved: vote-k selective annotation beat random annotation by 11.4 to 12.9% relative with similarity retrieval (random retrieval did not benefit); ReasoningBank distilled strategies beat raw-trajectory memory; AWM abstract workflows beat concrete example retrieval (+4.0 step success on Mind2Web vs Synapse).
agent_test: Store distilled strategy items vs raw traces and compare at equal prompt tokens.

claim: Adaptive or learned case selection adds a few points over plain similarity, which already gets most of the gain over zero-shot: CASCADE 66.68 vs NP-CBR 63.76 average over 12 tasks (preprint); Memento parametric vs non-parametric +0.6 at iteration 5; DS-Agent re-rank improves average rank 2.58 to 2.08.
agent_test: Add a cheap success-count or bandit bonus over base similarity and test the increment.

claim: Retrieved context is used unevenly and can hurt: a relevant passage in the middle loses over 20 points for GPT-3.5 (worst case below closed-book 56.1; oracle 88.3, verified); one irrelevant sentence leaves at most 18% of solved GSM problems consistently solved; high-scoring distractors hurt while random documents sometimes helped (+35% in one setting). All 2023-24 models. Update: Yoran et al. 2024 found a random retrieved passage cut Llama-2-13B accuracy by over 10 points on average and even top-1 Google retrieval hurt on 2 of 5 tasks.
agent_test: Put the best case first or last; add a distractor-case control to every retrieval test.

claim: Semantic similarity fails when relevance needs reasoning: the best MTEB embedder (59.0 nDCG@10) gets 18.3 on BRIGHT; reasoning-rewritten queries add up to 12.2. Cosine on learned embeddings can be arbitrary in theory (Steck et al.), shown for linear models only.
agent_test: Index cases by an LLM-written abstract of the problem structure; compare with raw-text keys.
audit_note: BRIGHT's 59.0 is the MTEB retrieval subset score, not overall MTEB.

claim: Many-shot in-context learning with fixed examples keeps improving to hundreds of shots on some tasks (Bemba +15.3%, Kurdish +4.5% over 1-shot) and degrades at 250 shots on one task, in contrast to agent case retrieval where k saturates early.
agent_test: Compare fixed many-shot vs retrieved few-shot at equal tokens, on non-agent tasks.

claim: Smyth and Keane adaptation-guided retrieval was opened: in a symbolic design system AGR found the most adaptable case 100% vs 70% (45 cases) and 12% (120 cases, 8 models) for similarity, and solved 3x faster (2.07 s vs 6.22 s). No LLM-era test of it was found. Richter, Bergmann and Weber local-global similarity papers and Tversky were still not opened. The only LLM-era weighted-attribute use found is CBR-RAG (+1.94% cosine over no retrieval, 32 test cases, hand-set weights, no clean ablation).
agent_test: Rank cases by estimated adaptation cost (edit distance to a solution for the new problem), not problem similarity.

claim: An LLM choosing cases directly matches k-NN choice only 20 to 28% of the time (Wilkerson and Leake as cited); source not located or opened. Update: second search this pass also failed to locate the figure; Hatalis et al. 2025 cite Wilkerson 2024 only for explanation and trust, so the 20-28% number is still unverified.
agent_test: Measure agreement between LLM-picked and embedding-picked cases and downstream accuracy of each.

claim: Recency-importance-relevance scoring in Generative Agents was never ablated term by term; only whole memory types were removed (full 29.89 vs no reflection 26.88 TrueSkill).
agent_test: Ablate the three retrieval terms separately on a long task.

claim: Adaptation-guided retrieval (rank by cost to adapt) beat similarity ranking in the classic symbolic test: the most adaptable case was chosen 100% vs 70% and 100% vs 12%, and total solving time fell from 6.22 s to 2.07 s per problem. Not tested with an LLM adapter.
agent_test: Rank k=5 candidate cases by an LLM-judged edit effort, then reuse the top one; compare against pure embedding rank at equal tokens.

claim: Letting memory grow without a quality gate hurts. Add-all lowered success vs a fixed 100-record memory in 4 agents (RegAgent 55.5 vs 67.5, EHRAgent 13.1 vs 16.8, AgentDriver 32.3 vs 40.1, CIC-IoT 59.9 vs 71.5, with 1050 records), while a strict ground-truth filter raised it (70.95, 38.5, 51.0, 85.4). Wrong stored runs propagate and widen the gap over time.
agent_test: Store a run only if an external check passes; compare against add-all with the same bank size cap.

claim: A retrieval gate has measured value. Question-popularity gating beat always-retrieve by 5.3 points on PopQA (GPT-3), retrieval hurt 10% of questions the model already knew, FLARE-style confidence gating plateaued at 60% or fewer retrieval steps and dropped past 50% on StrategyQA, and a trained complexity router beat fixed strategies on accuracy per time. All are factoid or multi-hop QA with 2022-24 models; no gate was tested for case reuse.
agent_test: Skip retrieval when top similarity is below a threshold or the cheap first attempt is confident; sweep the threshold and plot accuracy against retrieval rate.
audit_note: FLARE figures are percent of sentences triggering retrieval, 'plateaus above 60%'; claim wording 'plateaued at 60% or fewer retrieval steps' is loose.

claim: LLM-written abstracts of problem structure make better keys than raw text. Skill-KNN raised Spider execution accuracy from 74.6 (best raw-input) to 78.3 and kept above Random where raw SBERT-KNN fell below it; Buffer of Thoughts reports accuracy drops when its problem-distiller is removed, mostly on hard tasks. Neither isolates key type from stored content, and both use GPT-3 or GPT-4 era models on well-defined tasks.
agent_test: Index the same cases under raw text, LLM structure abstract, plan text and outcome; retrieve k=1 for each and compare at equal tokens.

claim: Utility-based pruning needs several retrievals per case: the history-based deletion rule used at least 5 retrievals and a utility threshold of 0.5 (0.3 to 0.7). On RegAgent it did not beat keeping everything (70.95 strict vs 69.80), with other agents reported to gain. A tiny bank of tens of cases will rarely give 5 retrievals per case.
agent_test: Track per-case outcome when retrieved; start pruning only after 5 retrievals; compare with recency-only pruning.

claim: The order of 4 in-context examples changes accuracy a lot for 2021-24 models: 24 permutations on SST-2 ranged from about 50% to over 85%; with GPT2-XL, TopK retrieval cut permutation variance (0.56 vs 0.90 for random) but did not remove it. Untested for 2025-26 models with 1 to 4 short retrieved cases.
agent_test: Run the same 4 retrieved cases in similarity order and reverse order; a gap under 1 point says position can be ignored.

claim: For GPT-3.5-turbo, self-generated analogous examples improve with count and K=1 is worst (GSM8K 76.1 vs 77.8 at K=5; MATH 34.8 vs 37.1). At davinci-003, 5 retrieved train-set examples scored 57% vs 54% for 5 fixed and 61% for self-generated; small models gain more from retrieval than from self-generation.
agent_test: Add a self-generated-analogue arm next to stored-case retrieval; it costs no bank.

claim: Several gaps stay open after two search passes: no random-case or no-case control for k=1 on a 2025-26 frontier model on multi-step tasks; no LLM adaptation-guided retrieval; no verified Wilkerson-Leake agreement figure; no weights ablation with correctness; no 2025-26 short-context position test. The last search pass was rate-limited, so absence is weak evidence.
agent_test: Run these as our own controlled tests; they are cheap, each needs about 3 arms.
